candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care > Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify assignments based on client needs; assign/delegate to personnel with appropriate competency and within allowable duties; evaluate staff ability considering competency, judgment and decision-making; establish priorities based on acuity.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — staffing skill mix, assignment, competency and acuity
candidate.educational_objective: Build a safe nursing skill mix by matching changing patient needs, acuity and workload with the authorized scope, competence, education, experience and available support of the nursing team rather than relying on head count, seniority or preference alone.

options.A: Base the staffing mix primarily on staff seniority and address competency differences after assignments are made.
options.B: Use the same staffing pattern throughout the shift even when patient acuity, workload, and required competencies change.
options.C: Base assignments primarily on staff scheduling preferences once the planned head count has been met.
options.D: Base the staffing mix on patient care needs, acuity, and workload, matched with each staff member's authorized scope or role, education, skills, competencies, experience, and relevant unit/support factors.

candidate.rationale: ANA staffing principles state that appropriate staffing is driven by the needs of the healthcare consumer or population and must account for patient acuity/intensity, workload, required clinical competencies, staff education, skill mix, experience, scope of practice, and characteristics/resources of the practice environment. Staffing plans must also be flexible enough to respond to changes in patient needs and care demands across and within shifts. Therefore D is correct. Seniority alone, a fixed staffing pattern, or scheduling preferences/head count alone do not address the patient- and competency-based factors required for safe staffing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe staffing and skill-mix decisions are dynamic and should match patient needs, acuity and workload with staff scope, education, skills, competencies, experience and relevant unit/resource factors rather than relying on seniority, preferences or fixed head count alone.
candidate.source_document_title: Principles for Nurse Staffing, 3rd Edition; Workforce Management
candidate.source_locator: ANA Principles for Nurse Staffing: staffing decisions are based on the number and needs of healthcare consumers/populations; population needs determine required competencies; staff should practice to license/education/scope/documented competence; staffing plans adjust to changes in care needs across hours/shifts/days. ANA Workforce Management: staffing resources consider patient care needs/acuity/intensity/workload together with staff skill mix, education, competencies, experience, unit variables and available resources.
candidate.source_version_date: ANA Principles for Nurse Staffing, 3rd Edition (2019) with current ANA staffing guidance live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A charge nurse is determining the appropriate RN, LPN/LVN, and assistive-personnel mix for a shift. Which factors should drive the staffing decision?
